svg.title: Gross move versus trading cost for short-horizon families and model cells
svg.desc: Seven short-horizon families and model cells, in basis points per round trip: the best gross move (blue) against the round-trip cost (orange). For six of them the gross move falls short of the cost: lead-lag 0.2 to 1.5 bp against 13 to 18 bp; order-book imbalance 0.4 to 2.7 bp against 4 bp; large sweeps 0.24 to 0.87 bp against 25.8 bp; the July 2026 short-horizon signal engine about 0 against 13.5 to 16.5 bp; a 4-hour gradient-boosted model 4.5 bp against 8.35 to 16.4 bp; pairs and basket reversion 5 to 16 bp against 16 to 51 bp. Only the 24-hour model, at about 22 bp, beat its 8.35 to 16.4 bp cost, and its net of +8.79 bp per trade had a t-statistic of 1.33, so it was inconclusive.
